newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm, upside limited.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm, upside limited.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended firmer on Thursday after finding good support below the key 18,000 points level, dealers said.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract finished 75 points higher at 18,130 after hitting a low of 17,960. Turnover was 19,000 contracts.

"There was not much interest (to sell) below the 18,000 level so we should hold above there for the time being," said a trader with a U.S. house. "We should consolidate around here for now," he added.
He said gains in export-related stocks underpinned the Nikkei cash and futures markets.
Dealers said the March Nikkei looked set to climb towards the 18,500 level.
"There is a little bit of strength in the near-term. The next resistance is in the 18,240-18,300 region but it's aiming to go higher, towards 18,545-18,575," said a dealer with a local institution.
On the downside, he said the market looked supported around 17,930-18,000.

He said Wednesday's Japanese newspaper report quoting a Bank of Japan official saying the central bank would keep interest rates low for the time being could have helped give the Nikkei a slight boost.

The March contract of the MSCI Taiwan index settled at 309.7 against their opening 306.0 on volume of 262 lots. Dealers said some spread trades were done in the June contract, which ended at 308.8 against 308.7 on volume of 15 lots.
